rationale: bugs_open/010 candidate (b). The Tier-4 tool-acceptance loop has no bound on repeated failure. Each acceptance verdict raises a FRESH improve_tool work item, so the fixer's per-item max_fix_attempts convention never engages across cycles — the item's own attempt_count is always 0 — and the only thing gating a retry is the 7-day verdict cooldown in check_tool_acceptance_due. A defect the one-shot fixer cannot solve therefore re-fails on a weekly cadence indefinitely, each time producing a materially identical fix, with no escalation and nothing recording 'we have tried this'. This was observed live: tool-loot-table-balancer on gamesdesign.co.uk accumulated FOUR complete improve_tool cycles against the same failing criterion (mobile-fit) between 2026-07-17 and 2026-07-18, and has never produced a passing Tier-4 verdict (zero acceptance-run notes). Candidate (a) of the same bug — drill-down overflow attribution — is already live and did improve the fixer's aim; a later diagnosis (bugs_open/024) found that the re-verifications were additionally testing an UNCHANGED page, which explains why those particular cycles repeated. Both of those are fixes to why the loop was not converging; neither bounds the loop when it genuinely cannot. That is what this change adds: a loop that cannot converge should stop and ask a human, not spend credits weekly forever. The change is deliberately narrow — it adds a count and one branch to the existing failure path, changes nothing below the threshold, and fails open.

plan.summary: judge_acceptance_results has no memory across acceptance cycles, so an insufficient fix is re-attempted identically every 7 days forever. Add a bounded count of prior FAILED fix cycles for the criteria failing now, and at a configurable threshold (default 2) raise ONE acceptance_stuck item at needs_human_review carrying why_escalated, instead of an identical N+1th improve_tool item. Below the threshold nothing changes. A counting error fails open to the existing behaviour.

edits.rationale: The count IS the guard, and its three bounds are what make it measure non-convergence rather than history. Terminal statuses only: an item still open is the CURRENT cycle, not a past failure — counting it would escalate a loop mid-flight, and this is not hypothetical, an open improve_tool item exists on the benchmark tool right now (216ea5fe, status 'claimed', raised by another thread as a bugs_open/024 proof) and must not trip the guard. Since the last PASSING verdict: a green Tier-4 result resets the tally, so a criterion that regresses weeks later is treated as a new defect rather than inheriting an old count. Criterion overlap: a fixer that fixed X and left Y unfixed has not failed at Y twice. The item_key matches the one this judge writes below it, so the count sees the judge's own history and nothing else. jsonb_typeof guards the array cast because improve_tool rows raised by other paths carry no failing_checks (live: tool_health items do not).
edits.sketch:
func convergenceAttempts(ctx context.Context, db *sql.DB, function, siteID string, failedIDs []string) (int, error) {
	if len(failedIDs) == 0 {
		return 0, nil
	}
	var n int
	err := db.QueryRowContext(ctx, `
		SELECT count(*)
		FROM site_work_items w
		WHERE w.site_id = $1::uuid
		  AND w.item_type = 'improve_tool'
		  AND w.item_key = $2
		  AND w.status IN ('complete', 'failed')
		  AND w.created_at > COALESCE((
		        SELECT max(n.created_at) FROM doc_notes n
		        WHERE n.subject_type = 'tool' AND n.subject_key = $3
		          AND n.source = 'tool-acceptance'
		          AND n.categories @> '["acceptance-run"]'::jsonb
		      ), '-infinity'::timestamptz)
		  AND jsonb_typeof(w.spec->'failing_checks') = 'array'
		  AND EXISTS (
		        SELECT 1 FROM jsonb_array_elements_text(w.spec->'failing_checks') e
		        WHERE e = ANY($4::text[]))`,
		siteID,
		fmt.Sprintf("acceptance_fail:%s:%s", function, siteID),
		function,
		toPGTextArrayLiteral(failedIDs),
	).Scan(&n)
	return n, err
}

// toPGTextArrayLiteral is the package's existing helper (resolve_composition_helpers.go:403),
// reused rather than adding a lib/pq dependency the codebase does not carry.

edits.rationale: Count before the doc_note is written, so the note records what actually happened rather than claiming a fix was queued when none was. Fail open on a counting error: fail-closed would turn a transient DB error into a silently dropped fix, which is a strictly worse failure than one extra fix cycle. The threshold is step config so a workstream can widen it without a rebuild.

+	maxCycles := datahelpers.GetIntField(config, "max_fix_cycles", 2)
+	attempts := 0
+	if params.DB != nil && siteID != "" {

edits.rationale: The escalation replaces the improve_tool insert rather than accompanying it — raising both would leave the auto-loop running while also asking a human, which is the churn this bug is about. Status needs_human_review keeps it out of dispatch (load_work_item_actions.go:559 selects status IN ('triaged','approved')) and, because needs_human_review is NOT in idx_swi_dedup's excluded status list, the partial unique index holds the item open: the weekly re-verdict hits ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and leaves the one escalation standing instead of piling up duplicates. why_escalated is mandatory content, not decoration — an escalation whose reason a human has to reconstruct is the same dead end as no escalation.

Six sqlmock tests over the judge's failure path: escalates at the threshold (asserting the item_type in the SQL the action actually issued, its needs_human_review status, its own dedup key, the why_escalated reason, and that the doc_note stopped claiming an improve_tool item was created); does NOT escalate at 0 or 1 prior cycles; fails open on a count error; honours a configured threshold; the count query still carries each of its five bounding clauses; and an empty failing set short-circuits without querying. The escalation assertions were confirmed to FAIL against a deliberately disabled guard before being trusted — a passing test that cannot fail is not evidence.

grounded_in: bugs_open/010: 'Nothing bounds a non-converging fix loop. Each acceptance-fail raises a *fresh* improve_tool item (the item's own attempt_count stays 0; the 3-attempt cap never engages because each try is a new item). The only thing gating re-tries is the 7-day Tier-4 verdict cooldown (source='tool-acceptance'), so this will silently re-fail on a weekly cadence, each time producing an identical insufficient fix, forever — no escalation, no "we have tried this."'
bugs_open/010 verify step 2: 'With (b): force two non-converging cycles on any tool; the third fail should produce needs_human_review, not a third identical improve_tool item.'

tool_acceptance_actions.go (judge, pre-change): 'Failures: one acceptance-fail note + ONE improve_tool item carrying the criteria as acceptance_test (findings pattern; bounded by the fixer's max_fix_attempts convention).' — the comment asserts a bound that does not hold across cycles.

check_tool_acceptance_due.go:89-100 — the only existing rate limit: 'SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM doc_notes WHERE subject_type = ''tool'' AND subject_key = $1 AND source = ''tool-acceptance'' AND (categories ? ''acceptance-run'' OR categories ? ''acceptance-fail'') AND created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL ''7 days'')'
load_work_item_actions.go:559 — 'AND wi.status IN (''triaged'', ''approved'')' — so a needs_human_review item is never dispatched to an agent.

idx_swi_dedup (live): 'CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_swi_dedup ON public.site_work_items USING btree (site_id, item_key) WHERE ((item_key IS NOT NULL) AND (status <> ALL (ARRAY['complete'::text, 'verified'::text, 'rejected'::text, 'wont_fix'::text, 'failed'::text, 'unresolved'::text, 'cancelled'::text])))' — needs_human_review is absent from that list, so an open escalation dedups subsequent verdicts.

Live count on the benchmark tool 2026-07-20, the exact query this edit adds: 4. Discriminating probes on the same data: a synthetic green verdict at 2026-07-18 00:00 cuts it to 2 (the reset clause bites); an unrelated criterion returns 0 (the overlap clause bites); the open in-flight improve_tool item is excluded by the terminal-status clause (returns 1 when that clause is inverted).

Live: zero acceptance-run notes exist for tool-loot-table-balancer (four acceptance-fail notes, 2026-07-17 and 07-18) — the tool has never passed Tier 4, so the reset clause is correctly inert for it.

RUNNING_NOTES_travelling_docs 2026-07-19: 'Consequence for bugs_open/010: its non-convergence evidence — two RED re-verifications, two "materially identical" fixes — is explained by an unchanged page, not by a fixer that cannot aim. The drill-down (candidate a) was still a real improvement; the convergence guard (candidate b) would have fired on a loop that was never being given a chance to converge.'
plan.risks: 1) The most material risk is the one the NOTES entry above names: a guard that stops the loop can mask a DELIVERY defect rather than a fixer defect. On the benchmark tool the four cycles repeated because the fix never reached the page (bugs_open/024), not because the fixer could not aim. This guard would have escalated that — which is arguably correct (a human should look at four failed cycles) but the escalation says 'the fixer is not converging', which would have been a misleading summary of a rendering bug. Reviewers should judge whether why_escalated should be weaker/more neutral about the cause. 2) Threshold choice: 2 is inherited from the bug file's suggestion. Too low and a legitimately hard three-cycle fix gets escalated; too high and credits burn. It is config, so it is cheap to change, but the DEFAULT is what will actually run. 3) The reset-on-green rule means a tool that oscillates (pass, fail, pass, fail) never accumulates a count and never escalates — deliberate, but it is a real gap: flapping is a different pathology this does not address. 4) The count is scoped to item_key acceptance_fail:<function>:<siteID>, so improve_tool items raised by OTHER paths (tool_health, Tier-2) are invisible to it; a tool being fixed by two routes will under-count. 5) acceptance_stuck is a new item_type with no handler and no admin-dashboard affordance beyond the generic needs_human_review list; if nobody reads that list the escalation is a no-op that also stops the auto-loop, which is worse than the status quo for that tool. That is a genuine open question for reviewers: is an unread escalation better or worse than a weekly identical retry?
